fixes.explanation: It's true, baker. The text says Samson went down to Ashkelon and gave the clothes to those who had solved the riddle. Then, "…burning with anger, Samson returned to his father’s house…" He pays the bet first, and then he goes home.
The text never mentions an invitation from her. Samson says he has seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah, then asks his parents to get her for him as a wife. That's the whole message.
Bees, baker. Samson leaves the road to see the lion's carcass, and in it is a swarm of bees. That's an unexpected tenant. The honey comes along with them.

That's what he leaves out. The text says he "…did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass." His father and mother eat the honey he gives them, and he doesn't tell them where it came from. It's the second secret of the lion, baker.

That's what the riddle is about. The eater is the lion and the strong one is the lion. The something sweet is the honey Samson found in the carcass (Judges 14:8-9). And he never told his father and mother where that honey came from (Judges 14:9).

The feast is where he tells the riddle, not what the riddle is about. The sweet thing that came out of the strong one is the honey from the lion's carcass (Judges 14:8-9). The feast is just where the riddle gets told.
No one says the feast has to end. She comes weeping and says, "You do not really love me!" She also says he has not explained the riddle to her. The feast keeps going for the whole seven days.

Yes, baker. After Samson tells her, the text says "…in turn she explained the riddle to her people." Then, before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city say to Samson, "What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?"

The text doesn't say she goes to Ashkelon. Ashkelon is where Samson goes to get the clothes. What it does say is that his wife was given to one of the men who had accompanied him. That's all it says about her here.
